title: File surfaces need tabs: opening several files in a row shows only the last
description:
GH #1297.

Symptom: an agent opening several files in a row to show the user leaves only the LAST one visible; each open replaces the previous.

Source: openFile has no tab-vs-replace notion. UI_FILE_OPEN_MODES (shared/types/filesystem.ts:20) is only view|edit|diff — how the CONTENT renders. The command carries {path, mode?, filesystem?} (shared/ui-bridge.ts:20) and uiCommandDispatcher.ts:128 calls surface.openFile(path) on the single file surface, so consecutive opens overwrite. openPanel carries an explicit id so panels coexist; files have no equivalent identity.

Ask: multi-file representation (tabs) so opened files coexist.

Design notes: re-opening the SAME path must stay idempotent (no duplicate tabs); likely an open disposition (replace|newTab) defaulting to today's behaviour so nothing regresses; bound the tab count so a loop cannot open hundreds.

title: Automation seeds: host-owned seed list; worker_cap as the single source of slot count
description:
Follow-up to PR #1288, from an investigation that found no host seam exists (evidence preserved here).

FINDING (verified by grep): plugins/boring-automation seeds itself — its own onReady hook is the ONLY caller of seedStandingAutomations, and store.readSeedManifest() reads .agents/automation/manifest.json directly off the workspace root. apps/full-app/src/server/plugins.ts and packages/cli/src/server/modeApps.ts both register the plugin generically by package id with NO seed injection point. The only policy.yaml reader in the repo is apps/workspace-playground/src/server/factoryAgents.ts -> loadConfiguredAgentFleet.ts, which is the persona/seat loader — unrelated to automation seeding.

WHY IT MATTERS: the slot COUNT (worker-slot-1..3 in manifest.json) duplicates beadle.worker_cap in .agents/factory/policy.yaml. Today worker_cap is read ONLY by the orchestrator prompt (a hint an agent may ignore); the three manifest records are what actually enforce the cap (one active run per record). So the number lives in two places and only one of them is real.

TARGET: add an injectable seed source to the plugin (generic API — the plugin must NOT read factory config), wire a small host-side composition module in both full-app and CLI that reads policy.yaml, generates worker-slot-1..N + triage, and passes them alongside the manifest's genuinely-scheduled entries. Then manifest.json holds only cron'd automations and worker_cap becomes code-enforced. Constraints: slots stay separate automation records (structural cap); seeding idempotent; lowering the cap must not remove a slot with an active run; missing/invalid policy.yaml falls back to 3 with a warning, never crashes boot.

DO NOT trim the manifest before the generator exists — removing the four records with nothing generating them leaves the factory with zero worker slots.

title: PR 1: native Pi session creation and rename
description:
## GitHub
#775

## Delivers
Browser-memory New chat plus direct-local first-send handoff to one native Pi session/no wrapper.

## Contract
Before Send, browser owns an ephemeral `BrowserDraft` with no durable session ID. First Send carries an in-tab idempotency key and transitions `new → native_persisted(nativeSessionId) → prompt_submitted → reply_committed | prompt_failed | unknown`. On `native_persisted`, same-tab retry returns the same native ID. Browser/server restart is explicitly `unknown`; no automatic recovery is claimed. Assistant success gates rename only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Empty chat creates no durable session.
- First Send creates exactly one native Pi transcript and no wrapper.
- Persistence-success/response-loss retry returns one native ID; prompt failure and restart unknown states are explicit.
- Rename unavailable before first assistant reply and native afterward.
- Boring and pi resume show the same materialized session.

## Proof
`pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-agent exec vitest run src/server/harness/pi-coding-agent/__tests__/nativeFirstSend.test.ts src/server/pi-chat/__tests__/nativeFirstSend.test.ts src/front/chat/__tests__/PiChatPanel.test.tsx`; `pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-workspace exec vitest run src/app/front/__tests__/WorkspaceAgentFront.test.tsx src/front/chrome/session-list/__tests__/SessionBrowser.test.tsx`; agent/workspace typecheck and agent invariants; manual evidence `docs/issues/775/proof.md`.

title: PR 2a: binding core and first-send handoff
description:
## Delivers
Workspace-safe binding store/routes and first-send handoff. Bind immediately at `native_persisted`, not assistant success.

## Storage and auth
CLI store uses Workspace adapter at `.pi/tasks/session-links.json`, serialized read-modify-write, temp-file plus atomic rename, recovery after interrupted write, and no raw path access. Link derives workspace/principal from trusted host context and authorizes native ID. Unlink authorizes task binding/workspace/principal only and never loads a missing native transcript, allowing safe unlink without disclosure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Browser handoff returns `{ nativeSessionId, firstSendState, idempotencyKey }`.
- One `(workspaceId, adapterId, taskId, nativeSessionId)` binding persists idempotently on `native_persisted`.
- Same-key response-loss retry returns same native ID/binding; prompt failure does not duplicate it; restart unknown has no automatic binding/recovery claim.
- Concurrent link/unlink is serialized/idempotent and survives interrupted write.

## Proof
`pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-tasks exec vitest run src/server/__tests__/sessionBindingStore.test.ts src/server/__tests__/sessionBindingRoutes.test.ts`; evidence `docs/issues/776/proof.md`.

title: AC1-H engagement data-boundary hygiene
description:
## Goal and why
AC1-H engagement data-boundary hygiene: Compose contractor-global, caller-readonly, and engagement-local writable scopes; bind sessions/tool state/artifact provenance to engagementId and prove deny-by-absence with cross-customer canaries.

## Scope
Implement one coherent, reviewable PR only; preserve Decision 21–24, workspace-first authority, and the plan's no-pure-mode rule.

## Explicit exclusions
No scheduler, queue, registry/provisioner, control plane, generic policy framework, secret/raw-path output, or unrelated refactor. Do not silently widen this bead.

## Acceptance and proof
Add focused unit tests at the public seam and integration/e2e or host-proof coverage where this task crosses a runtime boundary. Run the package typecheck, targeted tests, and the exact plan acceptance gate; attach redacted command output/evidence to the PR.

## Risks / owner blockers
Blocked by contracting trigger and AC1-D; no workspace type, policy DSL, vector memory, live grant, or automatic learning promotion.

title: D1-006 owner gate: approve EU runtime privilege model or select another profile

Owner decision gate for D1-006 privileged runsc execution. This is a human decision, not a code bead: after D1-006a evidence exists, the owner selects the privileged-execution model or declines the EU-production exit.

The record must link the accepted D1-006a lifecycle/security/isolation evidence, state the chosen model and rationale, identify approver and date, and be committed in the named decision/review record. No implementation test is expected. It remains blocked until D1-006a is complete.

title: Orchestrator agent plugin: dispatch trigger + boring_fleet tool
description:
GH #1276. Plan (owner-approved gate 1): docs/factory/orchestrator-plugin-plan.md r2.

Scope:
1. boring-automation: add 'dispatch' to trigger union; add list/nudge/cancel operations; rename automation run -> dispatch run internally. Existing suite must stay green (blast radius of the rename).
2. plugins/boring-orchestrator (app/internal): boring.agent = boring-orchestrator, pi.skills plan/feedback/owner-gate/handoff, boring.server exposing boring_fleet (list/start/nudge/cancel) built OVER automation primitives, no lifetime logic of its own. Owner rulings: worker_cap 3; one nudge per bead per attempt then cancel+reclaim, 2 attempts then Steward; triage automatic from tick one including issue comments.

title: #1129 bounded retry-safe MCP ingress admission
description:
WHAT: Reconcile the existing managed-agent MCP edge with Decision 22 and harden admission. Make canonical AgentTask v2 the authoritative task identity/lifecycle/messages projection (edge-specific inline Markdown may remain delivery presentation, not a second lifecycle). Require idempotencyKey on both start tools: non-empty ASCII `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+`, at most 128 UTF-8 bytes; resolve a host-authorized StartAdmission before scoped dedupe containing trusted admission identity, agentTypeId, and a one-shot acquireTaskLease() closure but no gateway/artifact reader. After retained-key return/conflict/limits/capacity checks, reserve the new single-flight record, call acquireTaskLease() exactly once, and atomically transfer any acquired lease to that record; on acquireTaskLease() rejection remove the record reservation and decrement the reserved per-credential concurrency slot exactly once; Core guarantees rejected acquisition releases every active lease/binding/reference; cached environment generations may remain under canonical retire semantics. On package setup failure after a fulfilled lease, remove reservation, decrement concurrency, and call release() exactly once. Every canonical terminal state completed/failed/canceled/rejected decrements concurrency and releases the lease exactly once. Retained retries, conflicts, and admission rejections never call acquireTaskLease(). The record retains its lease only through terminal result/artifact collection and always releases it on success/error/cancel. Status lookups receive a separate reauthorized disclosure scope with no gateway/artifact capability; single-flight by credentialId/principal/workspace/agent/key + the exact current parseBrief-normalized bytes; reject changed payload. Add fixed-window per-credential admission with required options maxStartsPerWindow 1..10000, startWindowMs 1000..86400000, maxConcurrentPerCredential 1..100; the window starts on the first admitted new start and resets when now >= windowStart + startWindowMs; rate rejection returns bounded retryAfterMs to that reset; dedupe before limits; increment only for new starts and release concurrency on terminal. Cap each fully serialized progress notification (including progressToken and framing) at 4 KiB and all emitted+retained serialized progress notifications for one delegation at 64 KiB plus 100 items; once exhausted, emit/retain one bounded coalesced marker and no further progress notifications; compact text projection; before passing parsedBody to the SDK, reject JSON-RPC batch arrays entirely (one request/notification object per HTTP transport call), then validate every response-bearing JSON-RPC request id: permit only a safe integer or an ASCII `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+` string of at most 128 UTF-8 bytes; reject null, unsafe/non-integer numbers, oversized/other strings, arrays, and objects before MCP dispatch. Notifications without id remain allowed. Also validate params._meta.progressToken when present with the same safe-integer or <=128-byte safe-ASCII rule; invalid/null/object/array tokens reject before SDK dispatch. Add exact final serialized-response cap MAX_MCP_STATUS_RESPONSE_BYTES = 2112 * 1024 bytes. Worst-case JSON budget: 32 KiB brief * 6 = 192 KiB; canonical 96 KiB final * 6 = 576 KiB; retained compatibility final projection 96 KiB * 6 = 576 KiB (derive from canonical task, no second lifecycle); 256 KiB validated Markdown * 2 = 512 KiB; all bounded task/delivery metadata = 128 KiB (including new 4 KiB artifact-title cap); all emitted+retained progress notifications measured after complete JSON/SSE serialization (including bounded progressToken) = 64 KiB; MCP/JSON-RPC envelope + compact summary = 64 KiB; total 2112 KiB, measured after complete serialization. Preserve the existing oversize-result test assertion: its 384 KiB title is rejected by the new 4 KiB title cap; do not weaken/delete it. Keep unexpired running/terminal idempotency records non-evictable until configured terminalRetentionMs; at capacity reject new work. Guarantee one session only while that record is retained in the same process; after TTL/restart duplication is explicitly possible.

PROOF PATH: pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-agent test -- src/server/mcp/__tests__/managedAgentDelegate.test.ts; pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-agent typecheck; pnpm lint:invariants. Tests cover AgentTask submitted->working->terminal projection/validation; zero lease acquisition on retained retry/conflict/rate/concurrency/capacity rejection; acquisition-rejection concurrency rollback relying on Core failure-atomicity; fulfilled-lease setup failure release + concurrency rollback; completed/failed/canceled/rejected exactly-once concurrency+lease cleanup; exactly-once lease transfer to a new record; task-lease retention through asynchronous delegate_task_start completion and guaranteed terminal/error/cancel release; status disclosure cannot access the task lease; per-request agent selection; exact/over key and bounds; same-key concurrent/retry/conflict; cross-scope; exact trimmed-brief identity; fixed-window boundary/reset; concurrency release; dedupe-before-limit; TTL/capacity behavior; maximum status through stock SDK client; exact/over and type cases for echoed JSON-RPC id and progressToken; batch-array rejection; progress emission/retention aggregate exact/over/coalescing, all proving rejection/bounds before tool/controller work.

FILE SCOPE: packages/agent/src/server/mcp/managedAgentDelegate.ts; packages/agent/src/server/mcp/managedAgentMcpServer.ts; packages/agent/src/server/mcp/__tests__/managedAgentDelegate.test.ts; package MCP exports only if required. No apps/full-app or Core files.

FITS ONE SESSION: yes; one package controller/server seam plus its focused test.

## Acceptance Criteria
Canonical AgentTask v2, not custom three-state status, is authoritative in structured responses; StartAdmission is capability-light and acquires no lease on non-admission paths; only a newly reserved task acquires one lease, releases it and rolls back concurrency on setup failure, and releases lease+concurrency for completed/failed/canceled/rejected, while each status disclosure is separately reauthorized; request-authorized agentTypeId is supported; one retained same-process scoped retry starts exactly one gateway session; changed payload and scope conflicts are stable; finite exact admission/progress/wire limits fail before model work; unexpired records are not evicted; existing brief/final/artifact caps and redaction do not weaken.

R2 OWNERSHIP/LIFETIME ADDENDUM: Keep one ManagedAgentMcpDelegateController at route-registration/process lifetime, but each McpServer + StreamableHTTPServerTransport is request-scoped and stateless (`sessionIdGenerator: undefined`). AgentApplication and Workspace hold no MCP connection/session. After delegate_task_start returns its receipt, HTTP/MCP disconnect must not cancel the background task; detach request-abort authority and retain a controller/task-owned shutdown signal. Synchronous delegate_task request abort still cancels, projects canonical canceled, and releases lease + concurrency exactly once. Controller close stops admission, aborts and awaits every in-flight task/terminal collection, releases every lease/slot, then resolves so the app may close its gateway. Admission/rate/concurrency keys by trusted credentialId, never TCP connection, SDK client, MCP session, JSON-RPC id, or bearer text. One client may start sequential/concurrent tasks; multiple client instances sharing one credential cannot exceed its fixed-window/concurrency/global caps. Add focused exact/over tests for same-client and two-client concurrency, async disconnect/reconnect polling, sync abort, controller close ordering/cleanup, completion/failure/cancel/reject cleanup, and restart/process-local loss behavior.

R2 REVIEW-FIX CONTRACT (supersedes conflicting lifetime wording above): The one-shot lease exposes only a bound task runner (run + stop), minimal reader, and release; raw AuthorizedAgentScope/full AgentGateway stay inside Core and the package cannot select another Agent, list/mutate unrelated sessions, or close the gateway. Async disconnect survival begins at the controller-observable atomic commit: attach lease + store running receipt before response attempt; pre-commit request abort cancels admission, post-commit uses task-owned cancellation and lost delivery is recovered by same-key retry. Both start tools single-flight to one task; first admission freezes origin mode/response behavior. delegate_task_start callers get receipts; delegate_task callers wait terminal; only the originating sync request can cancel a sync-origin task, while duplicate waiter abort is local. This slice proves package rollback for an injected acquisition rejection only; Core partial-allocation failure atomicity belongs to .4. Add required shutdownGraceMs 100..300000: close stops admission, aborts, waits grace, fences late status/artifact/task calls, logically releases lease/slot once at deadline, and resolves even for never-settling work.

title: #1129 bind MCP ingress to current Workspace AgentGateway authority
description:
WHAT: Replace full-app managed MCP compatibility dispatch with a binding-specific Core capability. At boot, full-app gives Core the server-owned credential binding (redacted credentialId + existing principal + workspace) and receives non-parameterized authorizeStart() and authorizeStatus() closures; authorizeStart() returns a capability-light StartAdmission (trusted identity + strict agentTypeId + one-shot acquireTaskLease()) and does not itself allocate a gateway/artifact lease; callers cannot supply another principal/workspace. Each authorization closure rechecks current app, non-deleted workspace, user existence/membership, strictly resolves persisted defaultAgentTypeId against the validated fleet (unknown persisted value fails stably; null may use the configured fleet default), and authorizeStart() returns trusted identity + resolved agentTypeId + one-shot acquireTaskLease(); only after package dedupe/limit/capacity checks does that closure return AgentGateway, branded AuthorizedAgentScope, minimum authorized Workspace artifact-reader operations, and release(). Acquisition is failure-atomic inside Core: if acquireTaskLease() rejects after partial allocation, Core releases every partial lease/binding/reference before rejection; no active task binding or capability survives. Existing cached environment generations may remain under the canonical environment manager and are disposed only by its existing retire policy; this slice does not change provider-cache lifecycle. Focused Core tests inject failure after each fallible allocation and assert exact reference cleanup/no active lease or task binding; cached environment generation count may remain unchanged until canonical retire. The package transfers a fulfilled lease to exactly one new task record or releases it on later setup failure; it retains the lease only through terminal artifact/result collection, then releases it. authorizeStatus() returns only the trusted disclosure identity needed to scope a retained record, with no gateway/artifact reader. Start/status consume that bundle and package request-time agent resolver; hostname/body/tool args remain non-authoritative. Reconcile current Core fallback drift with Decision 28 in the shared resolver/tests so web and MCP do not silently execute another Agent for an unknown persisted default. Keep route dark and fail startup without complete credential + fixed-window/concurrency config.

Start/status continue to reauthorize independently; connection closure is never revocation and does not select Agent/Workspace. title: R2b.3b: replica-wide runtime retirement and operation drain
description:
## Context
WorkspaceRuntime caches are process-local. A single host receipt cannot authorize provider destruction while another replica or accepted operation may still execute.

## Scope
- Register and heartbeat every Core-hosted WorkspaceAgentScope as `(appId, workspaceId, replicaId, leaseEpoch, expiresAt)` through a durable runtime-owner registry.
- Require each normal operation to validate the current owner lease; deletion fences prevent new owners and lease renewal.
- Publish the durable retirement job to every live owner, revoke passive streams with cursor reconnect, stop new work, and drain/cancel accepted request/background/dispatcher/tool work within bounded policy.
- Require every non-expired owner to retire and acknowledge the same fence epoch; allow offline owners to resume and acknowledge or expire.
- Deny stale owner resume/effects and keep provider/storage destruction blocked until all live-owner receipts settle.
- Provide the explicit single-process owner adapter for standalone/CLI.

- Branch retirement by durable classification: doomed Workspace drains every actor/owner and disposes the shared runtime; surviving Workspace targets only the departing actor's accepted/queued work and passive streams, records actor retirement receipts on each relevant replica, preserves collaborator work, and performs zero WorkspaceRuntime/AgentBinding/Workspace/Sandbox disposal.

## Constraints
- Active work remains non-evictable outside explicit authorized retirement.
- Expiry is not permission to resume stale work.
- This slice does not delete host transcripts/plugin state or finalize the Core user/provider.

## Proof
- Two live replicas, one offline then resumed, one expired owner, stale-resume denial, duplicate ack, timeout/retry, and all-owner barrier tests.
- Active/queued/passive stream drain and collaborator-continuity tests.
- Provider/storage destruction spy remains untouched until every required ack.
- Exact-once WorkspaceRuntime/AgentBinding/Workspace/Sandbox disposal.

- Surviving-Workspace tests run collaborator active/queued/stream work concurrently with departing-actor retirement and assert uninterrupted completion plus zero shared-runtime/binding disposal; doomed branch separately proves all-owner disposal.

## Acceptance Criteria
Every process-local owner and accepted operation is durably accounted for; stale replicas cannot execute and provider destruction remains impossible before the all-owner retirement barrier. Actor-only retirement in a surviving Workspace cannot stop collaborator work or dispose any shared runtime/binding/resource.

title: C3: durable idempotent typed Workspace creation and provisioning admission
description:
## Context
Typed products need explicit creation with server-stamped type and restart-safe admission; login/listing must never create implicitly.

## Scope
- Require client-generated opaque Idempotency-Key but never client workspaceTypeId.
- Persist unique operation under app, actor, expected type, and key with normalized payload fingerprint.

- Pass durable operation ID as provider idempotency key and expose pending/ready/error retry state.
- Narrow guarantees explicitly for providers that cannot deduplicate crash windows.

- Consume the trusted `allowWorkspaceCreation` value from CoreProductRequestScope at server admission; when false, reject direct/browser/replayed create requests before idempotency-operation, Workspace, membership, provider, provisioning, or runtime effects.

- Current Core create authorization remains authoritative.
- No duplicate Workspace/membership/provider resource on concurrent/restart/response-loss replay.

## Proof

- Direct-request and replay tests for `allowWorkspaceCreation=false` assert the stable denial code and zero operation/Workspace/membership/provider/provisioning/runtime writes or calls.

## Acceptance Criteria
Typed create is explicit, server-typed, replay-safe, and honest about external provider semantics. Server-side create admission enforces `allowWorkspaceCreation=false` with a stable zero-effect denial independent of frontend UX.

- `boring-bash` owns transport-neutral governed file/search/watch/exec Environment operations and coherence; `boring-sandbox` owns Agent/Workspace-neutral physical backends. All surfaces use one canonical filesystem; no copy/sync.
- Reusable backend identity, invocation view, one-exec shell grants, and opaque model capability stay separate. Unsupported hosted physical enforcement fails closed.
- AgentApplications are service-shaped but in-process v1. No public non-default selector, remote transport/discovery, distributed tasks, or contracted-agent policy.
- Preserve authored-source safety, history/delete/ownership and lifecycle fencing. Stable errors. No file deletion without explicit written approval.

## Scope
Replace final Agent-owned Workspace/Sandbox provider boundary with neutral backend handle for provisioning, canonical storage, exec, physical bindings, health/invalidation, persistence/cleanup; retain old exports during expansion. Ratify direct/bwrap/Vercel source of truth, locality, ops, physical binding/network, durability/watch/eligibility from code/tests. Every requirement is physical/advisory/unsupported. Hosted requires physical and fails stable unsupported when absent; direct/advisory is trusted-local unrestricted only. Remote staging may seed but never hide sync.
## Acceptance Criteria
Provider matrix + hostile tests prove actual mechanics, neutral imports, Vercel canonical-data ruling, direct/bwrap negatives and hosted network fail-closed. Sandbox test/typecheck/build + common gates; `F2A-PROVIDER-PROOF.md`.
## Review
Provider, thermo, security.
## Rollback
Old exports/selection stay; no canonical data mutation.
## Common execution rule
Run focused tests plus applicable `pnpm audit:imports`, `pnpm lint:invariants`, `pnpm check:golden-path`, and `git diff --check`. Record commands/exits/files/artifacts in the named proof. Use an isolated `.worktrees/` branch and keep the Bead `in_progress` until its implementation PR merges.

title: CLI must start in a normal project folder: stop resolving pi runtime from workspace node_modules
description:
GH #1283 (related #1237).

Symptom: boring-ui <pnpm-monorepo-folder> boots and reports ready, but every seat's tools 500 with PATH_SYMLINK_ESCAPE on <workspace>/node_modules/@hachej/boring-pi. Product looks healthy, is inert.

Root cause: the CLI prefers the WORKSPACE's node_modules for the pi runtime package. In any pnpm workspace that path is a symlink, so the guard rejects it. A clean pnpm install also produces a symlink, so no from-source checkout can be a workspace root today. Confirmed by contrast: a checkout with no node_modules works (falls back to the CLI's own npx install).

Fix, in order:
1. Never resolve the pi runtime from the workspace node_modules; always use the CLI's own install. Also closes a supply-chain hole (a workspace can substitute the runtime today).
2. For real workspace resources (.pi/skills etc.), check CONTAINMENT of the resolved target rather than banning symlinks. That is the actual security property; #1260/#1263 were reaching for it before #1264 reverted.
3. Fail at startup with a non-zero exit and the remedy in the message, instead of a ready hub whose seats 500 on first use.

Why now: the factory runs from a throwaway sibling worktree with no node_modules purely to dodge this, which puts all worker output outside the served workspace root so nothing is visible in the UI. Fixing (1) retires the workaround.

Note: EXCLUDED_DIRECTORIES already excludes node_modules from the resource WALK — this is the runtime-package RESOLUTION path, a different code path.

title: Vertical agents — Swiss SMB product line
description:
Parent epic for the Swiss-SMB vertical-agent product line (see GitHub issue #1210, docs/issues/1210/plan.md).

Thesis: ONE product, verticals are CONFIGURATION not code. title: Automation seeds need a seed_key column (kills the 997-key scan + UUIDv5 bit-twiddling)
description:
From the thermo review of PR #1288 (finding 2.3), deferred as a follow-up because it touches a migration.

PROBLEM: seed identity is persisted ONLY as a hash-derived UUID (postgresStore.ts:459-465, hand-rolled UUIDv5 bit-twiddling), so seeds cannot be enumerated. pruneSurplusWorkerSlots (factoryAutomationSeeds.ts:92-96) therefore GENERATES up to 997 synthetic keys per boot (MAX_FACTORY_WORKER_CAP - workerCap, 997 at the default cap of 3), SHA-256s each into a UUID, and ships them as a 997-element '= ANY(array)'. Generate-and-test standing in for 'list the seed keys that exist'. It also contorts findExistingSeedKeys into a key->id->query->id->key round trip plus a workerSlotIndex regex to recover what the caller already knew.

FIX: add a seed_key column. Then ensureSeededAutomation, listSeedKeys() (replacing findExistingSeedKeys) and removeSeededAutomationIfIdle become direct; prune becomes existing.filter(i => i > cap); deterministicSeedId, workerSlotIndex and the candidate array all disappear.

Note: the thermo review made filing this a CONDITION of deferring it.

AC1-D durable in-process subagent dispatcher: Implement one subagent pipeline with depth=3, full-ancestry cycle rejection, durable input-required state/deadline/idempotency, recovery scan, ephemeral live waiter timer, actor/principal audit, and Pi-session reuse.

## Scope
Implement one coherent, reviewable PR only; preserve Decision 21–24, workspace-first authority, and the plan's no-pure-mode rule.

## Explicit exclusions
No scheduler, queue, registry/provisioner, control plane, generic policy framework, secret/raw-path output, or unrelated refactor. Do not silently widen this bead.

## Acceptance and proof
Add focused unit tests at the public seam and integration/e2e or host-proof coverage where this task crosses a runtime boundary. Run the package typecheck, targeted tests, and the exact plan acceptance gate; attach redacted command output/evidence to the PR.

## Risks / owner blockers
Blocked by accepted AC1-D-SPEC and AC1-T2; no queue, broker, state-machine library, retry policy, A2A wire transport, or contracted mode.

title: Stop must not delete queued messages
description:
GH #1295.

Symptom: clicking Stop with messages queued discards the whole queue. User-typed content lost, no undo, no warning.

Code: both primitives already exist. interrupt (harnessPiChatService.ts:525) halts the turn and KEEPS the queue. stop (:519) halts AND clearAllFollowUps, returning the discarded messages as clearedQueue. The Stop button is wired to stop. The client receives the deleted messages and drops them (remotePiSession.ts:274 dispatches clear-optimistic-followups) — the recovery data is in hand at the moment it is discarded.

Fix: (1) wire the Stop button to interrupt — no new primitive needed; (2) make queue clearing a separate explicit affordance; (3) make any clear recoverable by restoring clearedQueue to the composer in order, or offering 'N messages removed — Restore'.

Keep stop available for host-side teardown; this is about what the button means. Same class as wt-391-forward-9jxj (#1290): UI diverging from what the session actually did.

title: D1-004e recoverable unused-binding rollback fence
description:
## Goal and why
D1-004e recoverable unused-binding rollback fence: own the append-only rollback journal, sorted advisory-lock protocol, durable prepare record, and tuple-based recovery rules for unused additions. It defines and tests an injectable activation/served-ack protocol but does not wire a stable core or publish a production collection pointer.

## Scope
One reviewable PR. Preserve Decisions 21–24, workspace-first authority, and no pure mode. D1-005c consumes this journal protocol to perform concrete preloaded-core swap, durable pointer publication, ingress-last start, and served acknowledgement.

## Explicit exclusions
No stable-core preload/swap implementation, production collection-pointer write, ingress wiring, reconciler daemon, delete/update of journal rows, or unrelated refactor.

## Acceptance and proof
Focused unit/integration tests prove append-only prepare/recovery tuple behavior, sorted lock ordering, and fail-closed unknown combinations through the injectable protocol.

## Acceptance Criteria
See acceptance field: focused proof verifies only this bead's owned contract.
acceptance_criteria:
Tests prove append-only journal and fail-closed tuple recovery for unused additions; concrete stable-core activation and served acknowledgement remain exclusively D1-005c scope.

Owned stable codes: D1_ROLLBACK_JOURNAL_FAILED (must match these names exactly — do not invent variants).
close_reason: Superseded by Decision 25 and the static package-first #391 plan after PR #794 physically removed obsolete AgentHost assets; do not dispatch or restore the former D1 path.

title: Mobile: split the 4.3MB eager entry bundle
description:
GH #1303.

Measured on the running hub (0.1.98): entry assets/index-*.js = 4,272,967 B uncompressed (1,252,291 B brotli); all JS referenced from index.html = 5,005,393 B; CSS 304,944 B; 20 eager modulepreload tags; single <script type=module> entry; brotli + immutable caching already in place.

Transfer is not the bottleneck — CPU is. ~1 MB/s parse on a mid-range phone means seconds of blocked main thread before first interaction, recurring on every cold start because parse/compile is not cached. One immutable 4.3MB chunk also means a release invalidates everything at once.

Causes visible in the asset list: no meaningful code splitting (d3 array/line/path and rough.esm — charting/Excalidraw deps — load before first paint), and 20 eager modulepreloads defeat splitting even once introduced.

Work, in order: (1) split the entry around the mobile critical path (chat first; workbench, file panels, Excalidraw, charts, plugin fronts behind dynamic imports); (2) preload only first-paint chunks; (3) CI bundle budget (fail if entry chunk > ~1MB uncompressed) so it cannot regress.

Related: Chrome 6-conn-per-origin vs per-workspace streams makes a slow start present as a hang; confirm after the bundle work.

title: Hide the legacy default agent and the Agent nav tab when a fleet is composed
description:
GH #1296.

Symptom: a fleet workspace lists 4 agents — 'default' labelled 'Agent', plus the three real seats — and shows an 'Agent' tab in the left nav that only makes sense with a single agent.

Source: resolveDefaultAgentFleet.ts:85 always prepends LEGACY_DEFAULT_AGENT_FLEET even when BORING_AGENT_FLEET=1 composes a real fleet. Label hardcoded at createAgentHost.ts:746 and embeddedGateway.ts:254 as ('legacyDefault' in agent ? 'Agent' : agent.definition.label).

Asks: (1) left-nav Agent tab only when exactly one agent; (2) the legacy entry must not present as a peer of authored seats — hide it from listings when a configured fleet exists, or label it 'default'.

CONSTRAINT: do not drop the default agentTypeId. Existing sessions bind to it and hosts normalize default -> primary (Decision 30). Keep it resolvable for existing sessions and API callers; change presentation/navigation only.

Same family as wt-391-forward-9jxj (#1290) and wt-391-forward-wul5 (#1295): the UI asserting something the system is not doing.

title: Approve Job Thread v0 plan + 8 owner rulings
description:
Owner must rule on all 8 open questions in §9 of docs/plans/multiagent-shell/job-thread-plan.md (PR #1403, round 2) before any Job Thread v0 implementation slice (S1-S5) starts. Verbatim:

1. The noun. Q1-A projection descriptor with a distinct noun (JobProjectionV0, recommended, R-c untouched) or Q1-B canonical multi-seat Thread (better end state; costs an R-c amendment, C7 Thread ownership, seatId-in-C7 pulled forward, and a #1355 ref rework)?
2. Relay vs native binding. D24 (:364) ratifies a native in-process agent-to-agent binding with input-required. v0 proposes the relay (no agent-facing capability, deletable, caps centrally enforced). Confirm the relay for v0, or build the ratified binding instead?
3. Attribution grade. Accept explicitly display-grade participantId for v0, or pull ratified C7 seatId forward now so the demo's audit story is envelope-grade?
4. Post/Run boundary. Confirm only settled final assistant posts + relay system markers cross seats — no tool calls, no intermediate messages?
5. Objective coupling. Is an Objective mandatory for a job? Confirm one-way ref with clientRequestId compensation, or should Objective gain a threadId?
6. Context and budget. Confirm oldest-first truncation with no summarization, and confirm that per-Thread spend is out of v0 (it needs a job dimension on MeteringRunScope, §3)?
7. Level D. v0 ships against Level B with the §4 limitation accepted. Complete Level D conformance (streaming lane #1009) now, or defer?
8. Acceptance bar. Confirm fixture-driven acceptance as the gate, with the live-model walkthrough labelled a non-deterministic smoke check?

Proof: owner sign-off recorded (comment or linked decision) answering all 8, with any Q1-B / Q2-native-binding / Q3-seatId / Q7-LevelD choice reflected back into the plan before S1 starts.

[2026-08-26] Plan docs reorganized as a pack: docs/plans/multiagent-shell/ (shell-plan.md, job-thread-plan.md, chief-of-staff-delta.md + *-review.html). Paths above updated; line-number citations are unchanged (files moved verbatim).

=== RE-SEQUENCING RULING — 2026-08-26 (owner) ===
This gate is now PREMISE-GATED and several of its 8 rulings are answered or superseded. Full program: docs/plans/multiagent-shell/premises.md

1. ENGINE SEQUENCING IS PREMISE-GATED. The engine does NOT ship on conformance Level B. It waits for P1 (Level D conformance + durable streams default-on, bead wt-391-forward-9p50). Q7 is RULED: wait for it, do not accept the Level B limitation. The interim Level-B receipt machinery in S1/S3 (JobRelayReceiptV0 chain, idempotent re-dispatch, crash-recovery ordering) is marked descoped-pending-P1 — not deleted; the post-P1 design decides how much survives on a durable substrate.

2. THE STORAGE QUESTION IS DEFERRED TO P2 FINDINGS. Q1 (the noun: JobProjectionV0 projection descriptor vs canonical multi-seat Thread) is WITHDRAWN as a plan-level recommendation and SUPERSEDED by premise P2 — a thread-storage spike plus competitor study (bead wt-391-forward-shell-ngfs.13, full brief in its body). S1 cannot start before P2 reports: P2 decides whether JobProjectionV0 is the right shape at all.

3. AUDIT-GRADE ATTRIBUTION RULED. Q3 is RULED: who-said-what is audit-grade from day one. Display-only participant chips are REJECTED. Section 8's honest concession — participantId as a display handle with no audit weight — is rejected as a shipping position. C7 seat storage is pulled forward as premise P3 (bead wt-391-forward-shell-ngfs.14).

4. RELAY vs BLACKBOARD IS A POST-P1 DECISION. Q2 is DEFERRED, not answered. Both candidates remain live. The Buzz / Grok Bot research (recorded in #1399) stands and does not need redoing. Level D is what makes the blackboard shape possible, so the choice is taken when the substrate is real.

5. NEWLY RULED: Thread <-> Objective is an OPTIONAL ONE-WAY LINK. An Objective is not mandatory for a job. (Q5 RULED.)

6. UNCHANGED BY THIS RULING: the posts-only conversation boundary and the shared-workspace artifact boundary (Q4 RULED, confirmed); truncation-only context with no summarization (Q6 RULED, confirmed); fixture-gated acceptance with live model runs as a labelled smoke check (Q8 RULED, confirmed).

REMAINING FOR THIS GATE (per premise P6, after P2 reports): re-rule what P2 answered and drop what the interview already ruled. Expected residue: the storage decision itself (from P2's report) and the relay-vs-blackboard choice (post-P1).

title: Job Thread v0 S1 — projection contract + store + edge allocator
description:
WHAT: projection contract + store + edge allocator. JobProjectionV0, JobParticipantV0, JobRelayEdgeV0, JobRelayTransitionV0, JobChainStateV0, JobCursorV0 schemas; file store with revision CAS, lock, atomic rename, load diagnostics; and the openEdge() allocator — one locked mutation that allocates turnOrdinal, mints requestId, reserves chain counters, and appends the pending edge. Append-only enforced. No relay, no UI, no agent tool.

Blocked by (plan §7): owner ruling on Q1 (noun); PR #1401 merged. [External precondition — PR #1401 is open; beads cannot depend on PRs, tracked here as a precondition, not a bead dependency.]

Scope: plugins/job-threads/src/shared/{types,schema}.ts, src/server/{jobProjectionStore,edgeLog}.ts + tests.

Proof: pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-job-threads test -- src/server/__tests__/jobProjectionStore.test.ts src/server/__tests__/edgeLog.test.ts src/shared/__tests__/schema.test.ts; pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-job-threads typecheck.

Negative proof: concurrent openEdge() calls never allocate same turnOrdinal and never double-reserve a cap; ordinals sort numerically (1,2,10, not 1,10,2); any attempt to mutate a written edge or transition is rejected; grep -r "seatId\|threadId" plugins/job-threads/src returns nothing.

Note: markerOrdinal is now DERIVED from transition append-index (openEdge no longer mints it) — S1's allocator scope shrank slightly there.

Note: flagged at the upper edge of one-session sizing — if the executor finds it oversized, split the allocator into its own bead rather than stretching the session.

title: Job Thread v0 S2 — actor-scoped dispatch + handoff tool
description:
WHAT: actor-scoped dispatch + handoff tool. Relay turn function over runWithWorkspaceAgent (per-invocation agentTypeId); handoff({to, message}) tool registration; dispatch keyed by the pre-allocated edge.requestId, with onAccepted appending the accepted transition. No chain logic yet.

Blocked by (plan §7): S1.

Scope: plugins/job-threads/src/server/{relayTurn,handoffTool}.ts + tests.

Proof: pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-job-threads test -- src/server/__tests__/relayTurn.test.ts; pnpm lint:invariants.

Negative proof: the lease-bound capability is not retained past the callback (test asserts use after return throws); no `new EmbeddedAgentGateway` anywhere in the plugin; a dispatch is never issued without a pending edge already durable.

title: Job Thread v0 S3 — relay state machine + recovery
description:
WHAT: relay state machine + recovery. Chain advance on settled turns, willRetry filtering, posts-only crossing, split cursors (consumed-source vs delivered-context), caps scoped to chainId, context bound with truncation marker, every row of §2's failure table, and the 4-step recovery order from §3 (ledger/snapshot reconciliation before outcome-unknown).

Blocked by (plan §7): S2.

Scope: plugins/job-threads/src/server/{relayChain,recovery}.ts + tests (scripted adapter).

Proof: pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-job-threads test -- src/server/__tests__/relayChain.test.ts src/server/__tests__/recovery.test.ts.

Negative proof: crash-after-accept re-dispatches the same requestId and yields duplicate:true rather than a second post; a destination that settled and emitted a handoff before the crash is processed, not skipped; outcome-unknown is never appended without steps 1-3 having run; a new human turn opens a fresh chainId without inheriting or resetting the prior chain's counters.

title: Job Thread v0 S4 — front projection (merged timeline)
description:
WHAT: front projection. Per §4's continuity principle, this is an adapter, not a new view: a message-source adapter feeding the existing PiChatPanel a merged (turnOrdinal, seq, markerOrdinal) stream (§3), plus the three additive marks — per-message agent chip, quiet inline joined/handoff/left system lines, ask-user join on the full triple against the existing block idiom. Drill-down links. No new timeline/list component, no Console pane changes.

Blocked by (plan §7): S3.

Scope: plugins/job-threads/src/front/{jobMessageSource,agentChip,systemLineMarkers}.ts + tests — smaller than a parallel view: no new render tree, no new list component.

Proof: pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-job-threads test -- src/front/__tests__/.

Negative proof: an ask-user hint whose triple matches no participant renders nowhere and answers nothing; a single-seat job renders byte-for-byte through the unmodified PiChatPanel path.

title: Job Thread v0 S5 — K7 demo fixture
description:
WHAT: K7 demo fixture. Two-agent fleet, scripted adapter acceptance asserting the §5 sequence, Objective compensation path, plus a separately-labelled live smoke.

Blocked by (plan §7): S4; PR #1382 merged. [External precondition — PR #1382 (objectives plugin, plugins/objectives) is open; beads cannot depend on PRs, tracked here as a precondition, not a bead dependency.]

title: Complete Gateway Level D conformance + durable streams default-on (D29 re-evaluation)
description:
Owner direction (2026-08-25): durable streams will be adopted for our agents soon. This is D29's own named re-evaluation trigger arriving ('durable replay is load-bearing once concurrent multi-agent streams exist' — DECISIONS.md ~:472), pulled by the Job Thread v0 plan (PR #1403 Q7) and the v1 blackboard direction (issue #1399: thread-as-durable-stream + per-seat automation triggers, the Buzz-shaped end state with host-enforced caps).

description:

No allowlist flag exists. Only apps/full-app opts out; the local CLI runs default-on. This is the plan's FATAL-live finding; ratified as "RCE first", exempt from all sequencing.

1. Flip default to DENY at both assembly sites. CLI gains repeatable --allow-external-plugin <name> (names, not a boolean) + env BORING_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_PLUGINS=a,b for CI.

title: A7: invocation-scoped ModelCredentialResolver — kill the BYOK bypass (F-33-G15)
description:
TODAY (verified): model invocation never consults workspace BYOK. packages/agent/src/server/harness/pi-coding-agent/createHarness.ts:591-596 builds AuthStorage.create()/ModelRegistry.create(authStorage)/registerConfiguredModelProviders(...) from AMBIENT host pi auth inside createPiSession. Process-cached ambient scans at routes/models.ts:68-70 and cli.ts:145-147; provider config from host env (modelConfig.ts:231). The credential vault (packages/agent/src/server/credentials/{hostResolver,withResolvedCredential,vault}) exists with ZERO production call sites — exactly the plan's undecided wire-or-replace state. This bead takes the WIRE-IN arm (ratified: wire in or replace explicitly, never delete-only).
DELTA:
1. ModelCredentialResolver seam at harness creation. Resolution order: invocation-scoped grant (workspace BYOK) → host-local explicit mode. Ambient ~/.pi/agent/auth.json is legal ONLY when the composition declares credentialMode:'host-local' (CLI single-user default); NEVER in workspace/core hosts.
2. Workspace/core hosts construct the resolver from workspace credential storage; missing BYOK → typed insufficient-credential refusal, not silent host-key spend (BYOK-user-first ruling).
3. models route + CLI caches keyed by resolved credential scope, not process-global.
4. Tripwire lands WITH this bead: CI grep gate — no AuthStorage.create outside the resolver module.
ROLLOUT: staged like P0.6 — resolver lands defaulting hosts to their current behavior via explicit credentialMode, then workspace/core flip to grant-required next release. Hand-run smoke on live dev deployment before enforce.
AC: (a) fake-provider test: workspace with BYOK → invocation uses it (assert key fingerprint); (b) workspace without BYOK → refusal, host key NOT touched; (c) CLI host-local UX unchanged; (d) grep gate green.
REFUTATION: if pi 0.80.x blocks per-invocation injection, fall back to per-session resolver at session build + epoch invalidation on credential change; record the deviation in this bead. Rollback: credentialMode:'host-local' per host.
DEPENDS: A1 types extraction (typing seam).

Long-lived streams have no revalidation: ui-control uiRoutes.ts:189, agentPlugins routes.ts:76, and createInMemoryBridge.ts:53-56 is an unauthenticated subscriber Set. Zero epoch concept in the repo.

Rotation vs revocation: if disconnect-on-revoke hurts credential ROTATION UX, split rotate (new epoch, grace overlap) from revoke (immediate) — decide inside this bead with a test for each.
AC: mutation tests per host wiring (all 5): open stream → revoke → disconnect ≤1s, no further events; re-verify after revoke fails; unauthenticated-bridge hole closed (subscription requires verified scope).
DEPENDS: A1 (typing).
Est M-L. Route: Claude.

title: Approve multi-agent workspace shell plan + 13 owner questions
description:
OWNER GATE for the multi-agent workspace shell plan (docs/plans/multiagent-shell/shell-plan.md, PR #1409). No shell implementation bead is ready before this is answered.

Proof: an answered Human Intention linked to docs/plans/multiagent-shell/shell-plan-review.html and the exact PR revision.

THE 13 QUESTIONS (verbatim from plan section 7):

1. Routing/location ownership. Recommended: package owns ShellLocation state + navigate(); host owns URL serialization (section 3), consistent with WorkspaceAgentFront.tsx:274. Confirm, or make the host own location entirely?

2. Nav extensibility, and the Inbox paradox. The ruled IA is fixed and ordered, but Inbox itself arrives today as a plugin contribution - appLeftActions: [{ id: "inbox", ... order: 10 }] (plugins/ask-user/src/front/index.tsx:245). A closed IA either hardcodes a destination the plugin owns, or keeps a contribution point the IA claims to have closed. Named section slots (L2a's proposal), tools-rail only, or IA fully closed with Inbox promoted into the shell?

3. Library persistence. ConsoleCollection cannot hold saved views (section 5.4). Workspace settings, a new plugin store, or descriptor-local/unsaved for the first tranche?

4. Contextual chat beside a view - declared a post-v0 non-goal. Confirm. When it returns: ephemeral thread, attach-to-last-thread, or view-scoped session?

5. Export surface and semver posture. Recommendation is zero-or-one new public export (section 4.2b). Confirm the shell stays internal, or name the external consumer that justifies a public seam.

6. Search/palette scoping. Search is a nav domain AND Cmd-K is an existing chat-pane palette (WorkspaceAgentFront.tsx:2362). One palette scoped across five domains, or a domain-scoped Search page plus the existing palette? Traits row 4 assumes the latter.

7. Attention data source and polling cost. Five domains with counts/badges implies five subscriptions. What feeds them, at what interval, and what is the cost with the workbench and a live thread already streaming?

8. Classic-layout deprecation line. Three layouts is a real maintenance tax (section 4.1's matrix must be filled for all three, forever). Is classic on a deprecation path, and if so from when?

9. Chat-pane behavior in the shell (traits rows 4b, 6b, 6c) - confirm off for v0 for splitting, palette-open-in-new-pane, and multi-pane restore. Note splitting is ON in plugin-tabs today and turning it off requires trait-gating :2570, which is currently unconditional.

10. WorkbenchLeftPane vs Library. If the workbench re-homes as Library, what happens to today's mounts in ChatLayout.tsx:647-655 - kept for classic, or migrated?

11. Touch reachability. Flyouts are hover-driven; the spike never passes mobileShellEnabled, so the Sheet path (PluginTabsWorkspaceShell.tsx:138-163) is unexercised by every section 2 claim. Four columns and hover flyouts on a phone is unanswered.

12. Kanban. SAAS_VIEWS carries kanban descriptors with no kanban renderer in the repo (SaasSpike.tsx:688-700). In scope for Library, or deferred?

13. Nav supersession. Does this plan's fixed IA supersede #1355 Slice 3's left-pane organization for the workspace-shell layout, with Slice 3 retaining plugin-tabs? This is a #1409 decision, not a #1355 Gate 1 item (section 5.3).

title: P2 — Thread storage model: competitor study + technical spike
description:
PREMISE P2 of the multi-agent shell program (docs/plans/multiagent-shell/premises.md). The thread storage model is NOT decided; this spike decides it. The engine's "noun" question (JobProjectionV0 vs canonical multi-seat Thread) is WITHDRAWN as a plan-level recommendation and replaced by this premise. Engine S1 cannot start before this reports.

RESEARCH QUESTION: How do systems that successfully run long-lived, multi-participant conversations model the relationship between a durable conversation record and the individual sessions/runs inside it?

=== PART A — COMPETITOR STUDY ===
Study each system for the SAME SIX FACTS so answers are comparable:
1. What is the durable unit - the conversation, the message, or the participant session?
2. Is participation a property of the record, or a separate join?
3. How is per-message authorship attributed, and is it audit-grade or display-grade?
4. What happens to the record when a participant is removed - rewrite, tombstone, or retain?
5. How is "the same conversation" addressed across surfaces (deep link, API, search)?
6. What does archival mean - a flag, a move, or a different store?

SYSTEMS:
- Slack - channel + threaded replies at very large scale; the canonical "channel is the record" model
- Discord - threads as first-class children of channels; explicit archive semantics
- Linear - issue-as-record with a comment stream; closest to "1 Thread = 1 job"
- Intercom - conversation record with BOTH human and agent participants and handoffs; closest analogue to our problem
- Notion - blocks-as-records; discussion attached to arbitrary subjects
- Buzz - already researched (#1399): shared durable event log, no central record; the "no record at all" end of the spectrum

OUTPUT: comparison table on those six facts + a short verdict naming which model our constraints most resemble and why.

=== PART B — TECHNICAL SPIKE, IN OUR STACK ===
Build each candidate far enough to MEASURE, not to ship:
(i) INDEX-CARD / PROJECTION - a lightweight record pointing at existing per-agent sessions, projecting them into one timeline. Cheap to add; timeline is derived.
(ii) FIRST-CLASS THREAD RECORD - the thread owns its own durable message stream; per-agent sessions become an implementation detail beneath it.

MEASURE for each: write path complexity; read/replay cost for a long thread; behavior under P1 durable streams; how per-message attribution lands (feeds P3); what a participant change costs; migration cost from today's per-session records; what #1355's reference types would have to become.

=== DECISION CRITERIA — the spike is done when it can answer ===
1. Which model survives a restart with the timeline intact, with least new machinery on top of P1?
2. Which gives audit-grade attribution without a second ledger (P3's constraint)?
3. Which lets a Thread's participants change without rewriting or losing history?
4. Which requires the smaller migration from today's per-session records?
5. Which one can #1355 type its conversation references against TODAY, without assuming single-seat?

NOT IN SCOPE: shipping either candidate; the relay-vs-blackboard choice (post-P1); any UI.

PROOF: a written report answering the five decision criteria, with the Part A comparison table; the spike branch retained as evidence. This is a research/spike bead - its proof is the report, not a green test suite.

SIZING: 1 research session (Part A) + 1 spike session (Part B), runnable in parallel. Part B should not start before P1's shape is known (criterion 1 depends on it).

FEEDS: the engine gate (P6), engine S1, and #1355's ConsoleThreadRefV1 repair.

title: P3 — Seat storage / C7: audit-grade attribution
description:

The engine plan's section 8 already concedes the honest position: participantId values minted in the plugin are "temporary display handles ... not seatId, not envelope identity, and carry no audit weight", and ratified P0 puts seatId in C7. The owner has ruled that this gap does not ship.

WHAT: pull the ratified C7 seat-catalog work forward far enough that per-Run seatId is real envelope identity, and per-message attribution in a multi-seat Thread resolves through it rather than through a mutable display record. "seatId in C7" is already ratified P0 required (docs/plans/long-term/ratified/RECONCILIATION.md:153) - this premise is SEQUENCING, not new ontology.

PROOF: an attribution that survives a participant being removed; a test asserting no attribution path reads a mutable display field; the trajectory spine carrying seatId end to end.

SIZING: ~2 sessions, and genuinely uncertain - this is the premise most likely to grow once opened, because it touches the envelope.

UNBLOCKS: honest agent chips in the thread timeline (shell L4), drill-down provenance, and any later billing/metering per seat.

COUPLING WARNING: P3 and P2 are coupled - attribution shape depends on storage shape. Do not run these as independent spikes that each assume the other's answer. P2's decision criterion 2 exists to prevent the deadlock: the storage spike must report how attribution lands under each candidate.
